Local corpus analysis · 17 August – 17 September 2026 · UTC

Topic spikes & sentiment shifts

Full-corpus lexical topic counts and measured engagement trajectories, paired with author-balanced sampled text polarity. No Azure resources used.

Collection break, not a platform-wide trend. September has dramatically fewer collected posts. Topic spikes use share of each day's unique tweets and within-regime baselines. September 17 is partial and excluded from peak selection. This reduces—but cannot eliminate—collection bias.

    Genuine engagement growth

    Snapshot deltas are distinct from final popularity. Sampling intervals are irregular; a rate is an average between observations, not a measured minute-by-minute viral curve. Retweet-prefixed posts are not ranked as independent original engagement.

    Methods and limits

    • Full corpus: latest observation per numeric tweet ID; max(version, added_at), including ID groups spanning files. All hashtags discovered; 58 explicit, overlapping entity/keyword families additionally measured. This is not exhaustive semantic labeling of every tweet.
    • Traction: exact topic counts and distinct authors; displayed lift is peak share / other complete-day share in the same August or September collection regime. Entity topics also have a language-mix-adjusted sensitivity estimate.
    • Sentiment: whole-post positive-minus-negative model score, −1 to +1. Not stance toward the entity. At most 200 peak and 300 baseline authors; one post per author, normalized text templates capped. Replies/quotes included; RT-prefixed posts excluded.
    • Inference: CardiffNLP multilingual Twitter model. Primary tests only ar/de/en/es/fr/hi/it/pt. Other languages are exploratory. Sarcasm, code-switching, mourning and mixed-target text require caution.
    • Strong shift: minimum 80 supported-language authors per period and 80 in common language strata; |mean shift| ≥0.15; author-bootstrap 95% interval excludes zero; language-adjusted BH q<0.05; adjusted and raw signs agree.
    • Uncertainty: confidence intervals reflect sampling, not model calibration or the unknown collection process. Baselines are retrospective, not causal. Named-event claims in tweets are not externally verified. Media content is not analyzed.
